writeup.headline: Bloom Energy rates Hold: rapid growth and net cash offset by a very high valuation and weak cash quality.
writeup.thesis: Bloom scores 46, a Hold that sits only 2 points above the Sell line. Growth is the main support, with TTM revenue growth of 112.2% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 139.8% year on year, though growth slowed by 27.9 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 92 on a net cash position. Against that, valuation scores just 4: the shares trade at 17.7x sales and 118.8x EV/EBIT, both high in absolute terms, with an FCF yield 5.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and they are more expensive than at 52 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S. Quality scores 28 because free cash flow excluding customer prepayments is negative (an FCF margin of -4.4% versus a reported 11.5%) and the diluted share count is up 38.0% year on year.
key_risks: Cash flow leans on customer prepayments; FCF excluding them is negative, which drove the post-earnings selloff.
Heavy customer concentration: two customers made up about 69% of Q3 revenue, one a related party, and Oracle has issued a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter.
Valuation is high in absolute terms (17.7x sales, 118.8x EV/EBIT), leaving little room if growth keeps slowing.
Shareholder dilution, with diluted share count up 38.0% year on year, plus insider selling and no insider purchases over the past year.
Weak recent trend: price 34.0% below its 52-week high and shares 29.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days; a scandium-sourcing class action is still pending.
what_would_change: A 2-point drop in the score would move it to Sell, for example from further price weakness hurting trend, slower growth, or more negative news on customers or the Oracle project.
Reaching Buy needs 19 more points, which would most likely require positive free cash flow excluding prepayments to lift quality and valuation scores.
A clearly cheaper valuation, through a lower share price or much higher earnings and cash flow, would help the factor scoring just 4.
